reasons: The source explicitly gives this as an illustration: for leads worried about spam, send an email saying not to spam them and offering a link to choose their preferred email frequency.
The candidate appropriately treats this as an example rather than a universal implementation requirement.
Its claim and action accurately reflect the instruction to seed the product or service throughout what is being given to the lead.

Its unknowns field says the example is an "emailed website and marketing review," but the excerpt identifies a website and marketing review without saying that it is emailed. That delivery-method detail is unsupported by this excerpt.
The source directly says to map out the process needed to turn people into an actual sale after a form submission, rather than only creating a high-converting website.
The action does not add a required process format or unsupported completion threshold.
The excerpt calls an assessment the first step in its generic process and specifies that it should understand the scale of the person's problem and help identify a possible solution.
The candidate preserves both the sequencing and the stated purpose without inventing a delivery method.
The source expressly says unqualified leads will occur and instructs the listener to "Have a plan B."
It accurately characterizes the stated plan B as another way to monetize people who are not right for the main offering.
The claim accurately reflects the source's statement that becoming a lead does not remove fear of being pitched or making the wrong decision.
It does not assert that every individual lead has either fear as a measured fact beyond the source's generalized framing.
The source explicitly asks what leads are most scared of and how to immediately do the opposite of that feared thing.
The candidate properly notes that the excerpt supplies only one concrete illustration of the framework.
The excerpt directly links receiving no objections to a funnel that is not wide enough and says it needs to be expanded.
The candidate preserves the qualitative nature of the guidance and correctly avoids inventing a target conversion rate or funnel size.
The source states that making the lure more attractive brings more unqualified leads, while also bringing more qualified leads and therefore more sales.
The candidate states this as the source's principle and supplies no unsupported numerical claim.
The source warns that telling a team merely to call booked consultations, talk about whatever, and see whether leads sign up will go badly.
It accurately attributes that warning to the absence of needed structure and a script.

source_limitations: The excerpt begins mid-sentence and ends mid-sentence, so preceding context and the steps following the proposal are unavailable.
The material is spoken instructional content with anecdotal examples; it does not provide independent evidence that the proposed tactics or outcomes generalize.
The excerpt does not specify the actual assessment method, call questions, proposal format, email content, cadence, conversion target, or referral-commission terms.
